set_title: Lung signs on chest x-ray: Westermark sign, Hampton hump, Kerley B lines, Deep sulcus sign and Golden S sign
stem: A 61-year-old woman has sudden pleuritic chest pain and hemoptysis 5 days after hip replacement. Chest x-ray shows a wedge-shaped, pleural-based opacity in the right lower lung.
oneliner: 61F, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis after hip surgery + wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity → ?

whyNot.A: Westermark sign is focal lucency from reduced vessels, not a **wedge-shaped opacity**
whyNot.C: Kerley B lines are thin horizontal basal lines, not a **wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity**
whyNot.D: Deep sulcus sign is a lucent costophrenic angle, not an **opacity**
whyNot.E: Golden S sign is lobar collapse around a mass, not a **wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity**

why: Hampton hump is a wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity from a pulmonary infarct. **Hemoptysis and pleuritic pain after hip surgery** point to pulmonary embolism.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Focal clear lung from reduced vessels
Short horizontal lines at lung bases
Deep lucent costophrenic angle, supine film
Reverse S edge of collapsed right upper lobe
Central hilar mass causing lobar collapse

idea.rule: Wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity = pulmonary infarct from embolism.
also: Westermark sign is the lucent counterpart

set_title: Lung signs on chest x-ray: Westermark sign, Hampton hump, Kerley B lines, Deep sulcus sign and Golden S sign
stem: A 47-year-old woman has sudden dyspnea after a long flight. Chest x-ray shows a lung region with markedly reduced vascular markings and no visible pleural line.
oneliner: 47F, sudden dyspnea after long flight + clear lung zone, reduced markings, no pleural line → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Pneumothorax shows a visible pleural line, but here there is **no pleural line**
whyNot.B: Bullae reflect chronic smoking; hers is a **sudden dyspnea after a long flight**
whyNot.C: Aspiration is a pediatric concern; hers is **sudden dyspnea after a long flight**
whyNot.E: Congenital lobar emphysema presents in infancy; she is **47 years old**

why: Westermark sign is a focal area of oligemia distal to an embolic occlusion. **Sudden dyspnea after a long flight** with reduced markings fits pulmonary embolism.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Focal clear lung from reduced vessels
Short horizontal lines at lung bases
Deep lucent costophrenic angle, supine film
Reverse S edge of collapsed right upper lobe
Central hilar mass causing lobar collapse

idea.rule: Focal clear lung with fewer vessels after prolonged immobility = pulmonary embolism.
also: Seen on only a minority of embolism films

set_title: Lung signs on chest x-ray: Westermark sign, Hampton hump, Kerley B lines, Deep sulcus sign and Golden S sign
stem: A 70-year-old man has orthopnea and an S3. Chest x-ray shows thin horizontal streaks 1-2 cm long reaching the pleura at the lateral lung bases, with an enlarged heart.
oneliner: 70M, orthopnea, S3 + short horizontal streaks at lateral lung bases, big heart → ?

whyNot.A: Hampton hump is a wedge-shaped opacity; his film shows **short horizontal streaks**
whyNot.B: Westermark sign is focal lucency; his film shows **horizontal streaks at the bases**
whyNot.D: Deep sulcus sign is a lucent costophrenic angle, not **septal lines**
whyNot.E: Golden S sign is lobar collapse over a mass, not **basal horizontal streaks**

why: Kerley B lines are short horizontal lines from thickened interlobular septa filled with edema fluid. **Orthopnea, S3 and cardiomegaly** point to left heart failure.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Focal clear lung from reduced vessels
Short horizontal lines at lung bases
Deep lucent costophrenic angle, supine film
Reverse S edge of collapsed right upper lobe
Central hilar mass causing lobar collapse

idea.rule: Short horizontal basal lines = septal edema of left heart failure.

set_title: Lung signs on chest x-ray: Westermark sign, Hampton hump, Kerley B lines, Deep sulcus sign and Golden S sign
stem: A 66-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history has cough and hemoptysis. Chest x-ray shows right upper lobe collapse with a reverse S-shaped fissure.
oneliner: 66M, 50 pack-years, hemoptysis + right upper lobe collapse, reverse S-shaped fissure → ?

whyNot.A: Simple pneumonia consolidates without the **lobar collapse and S-shaped fissure**
whyNot.C: An effusion obscures the costophrenic angle, not a **collapsed lobe with a bulging fissure**
whyNot.D: Heart failure causes bilateral edema, not **unilateral upper lobe collapse**
whyNot.E: Pneumothorax shows a pleural line, not **lobe collapse with a reverse S fissure**

why: Golden S sign is a reverse S contour where a hilar mass bulges the collapsed lobe's fissure. **Smoking and hemoptysis with upper lobe collapse** suggest a central bronchogenic carcinoma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Focal clear lung from reduced vessels
Short horizontal lines at lung bases
Deep lucent costophrenic angle, supine film
Reverse S edge of collapsed right upper lobe
Central hilar mass causing lobar collapse

idea.rule: Right upper lobe collapse with reverse S fissure = central hilar mass.
also: Suspect bronchogenic carcinoma in a smoker

set_title: Chest exam findings: Egophony, Whispered pectoriloquy, Decreased tactile fremitus, Hyperresonance and Tracheal deviation away
stem: A 55-year-old man has fever and a productive cough with rust-colored sputum. Over the right lower lobe, he is asked to say 'ee' and the examiner hears 'ay'.
oneliner: 55M, fever, rusty sputum + 'ee' heard as 'ay' over the right lower lobe → ?

whyNot.A: Whispered pectoriloquy is clear whispered speech; here **'ee' sounds like 'ay'**
whyNot.B: Decreased tactile fremitus is a weak vibration; here **'ee' becomes 'ay'**
whyNot.C: Hyperresonance is a percussion finding; here **'ee' becomes 'ay'**
whyNot.E: Tracheal deviation is a position finding; here **'ee' becomes 'ay'**

why: Egophony is the change of spoken 'E' to 'A' over consolidated lung, which transmits higher frequencies. **Rust-colored sputum with fever** fits lobar pneumonia.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Whispers heard clearly through chest wall
Trachea pushed to the opposite side

also: Also heard above a pleural effusion

set_title: Chest exam findings: Egophony, Whispered pectoriloquy, Decreased tactile fremitus, Hyperresonance and Tracheal deviation away
stem: A 40-year-old woman has dyspnea. Over the left lung base there is dullness to percussion, decreased vibration on palpation and absent breath sounds.
oneliner: 40F, dyspnea + left base dullness, weak vibration, absent breath sounds → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Pneumonia increases fremitus and breath sounds, but here they are **decreased and absent**
whyNot.B: Fibrosis gives dry crackles and preserved sounds, not **absent breath sounds with dullness**
whyNot.D: Bronchitis does not cause **dullness and absent breath sounds**
whyNot.E: Asthma causes wheeze with hyperresonance, not **basal dullness and absent breath sounds**

why: Decreased tactile fremitus occurs when fluid or air separates lung from chest wall. **Dullness with absent breath sounds** localizes the problem to a pleural effusion.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Whispers heard clearly through chest wall
Trachea pushed to the opposite side

idea.rule: Dull, silent base with weak fremitus = pleural effusion.
also: Pneumothorax is also decreased but hyperresonant

set_title: Chest exam findings: Egophony, Whispered pectoriloquy, Decreased tactile fremitus, Hyperresonance and Tracheal deviation away
stem: A 19-year-old tall, thin man has sudden left pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea at rest. Percussion over the left hemithorax produces a drum-like note and breath sounds are decreased.
oneliner: 19M, tall, thin, sudden left pleuritic pain + drum-like percussion note on left → ?

whyNot.A: Egophony changes 'ee' to 'ay' over consolidation; his finding is a **drum-like percussion note**
whyNot.C: Whispered pectoriloquy is a speech-transmission sign; his finding is **percussion**
whyNot.D: Decreased tactile fremitus is a palpation finding; his sign is a **drum-like percussion note**
whyNot.E: Tracheal deviation is a position finding; his sign is a **drum-like percussion note**

why: Hyperresonance is an abnormally loud, low-pitched percussion note over air-filled pleural space or lung. **A tall thin young man with sudden pleuritic pain** suggests spontaneous pneumothorax.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Whispers heard clearly through chest wall
Trachea pushed to the opposite side

idea.rule: Drum-like percussion note with absent breath sounds = pneumothorax.

set_title: Chest exam findings: Egophony, Whispered pectoriloquy, Decreased tactile fremitus, Hyperresonance and Tracheal deviation away
stem: A 28-year-old man is intubated after a motor collision and becomes hypotensive with rising airway pressures. His trachea shifts to the left, neck veins are distended and the right chest is hyperresonant with absent breath sounds.
oneliner: 28M, ventilated trauma, hypotension + trachea shifts left, right chest hyperresonant → ?
ask: What is happening in the right chest?

whyNot.B: Hemothorax is dull to percussion, but the right chest is **hyperresonant**
whyNot.C: Atelectasis pulls the trachea toward the lesion; his shifts **away to the left**
whyNot.D: Mainstem intubation shifts the trachea toward the collapsed side, not **away with hyperresonance**
whyNot.E: Tamponade does not give **tracheal shift and a hyperresonant right chest**

why: A trachea pushed away from a hyperresonant, silent hemithorax signals tension pneumothorax, where trapped air raises pressure and impairs venous return. **Hypotension with distended neck veins** confirms it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Whispers heard clearly through chest wall
Trachea pushed to the opposite side

idea.rule: Trachea pushed away + hyperresonance + shock = tension pneumothorax.

set_title: Chest and airway signs: Hamman crunch, Hoover sign, Platypnea-orthodeoxia, Oliver sign (tracheal tug) and Pemberton sign
stem: A 68-year-old man with severe COPD has lower rib margins that move inward during inspiration. A chest x-ray shows hyperinflated lungs.
oneliner: 68M, severe COPD + lower ribs move inward on inspiration → ?

options.B: Rigid chest wall from ankylosing spondylitis

whyNot.B: Ankylosing spondylitis limits rib motion, not **inward rib movement with hyperinflated lungs**
whyNot.C: An effusion gives dullness and diminished breath sounds, not **hyperinflation with inward ribs**
whyNot.D: Ascites does not cause **inward lower rib movement with hyperinflated lungs**
whyNot.E: Phrenic palsy causes paradoxical abdominal motion; here the **ribs move inward with hyperinflation**

why: Hoover sign is paradoxical inward movement of the lower ribs on inspiration. In **severe COPD**, a flattened diaphragm pulls the ribs inward when it contracts.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Lower ribs pull inward on inspiration
Dyspnea and hypoxia when upright, better lying
Trachea tugs downward with each heartbeat
Face flushes when both arms are raised
Substernal goiter obstructing the thoracic inlet

idea.rule: Lower ribs moving inward on inspiration = flat diaphragm from hyperinflation.

set_title: Named triads II: Wernicke triad, Hakim triad, Plummer-Vinson triad, Meigs syndrome and Kartagener triad
stem: A 28-year-old infertile man has had chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis since childhood. Chest x-ray shows dextrocardia. Semen analysis shows normal sperm counts with immotile sperm.
oneliner: 28M, infertile, sinusitis, bronchiectasis + dextrocardia, immotile sperm → ?

options.A: CFTR chloride channel in epithelial cells
options.C: Kinesin in axonal transport of vesicles
options.D: Fibrillin-1 in connective tissue elastic fibers

whyNot.A: Cystic fibrosis causes absent vas deferens; he has **dextrocardia and immotile sperm**
whyNot.B: It causes emphysema and liver disease; he has **dextrocardia and immotile sperm**
whyNot.C: Kinesin defects cause neuropathy; they do not explain **dextrocardia with sinusitis**
whyNot.D: Fibrillin defects cause lens dislocation and aortic dilation; he has **sinusitis and bronchiectasis**

why: Situs inversus, chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis are Kartagener triad. **Immotile sperm** point to primary ciliary dyskinesia from defective dynein arms.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dysphagia, esophageal webs, iron deficiency anemia
Iron deficiency; raises esophageal SCC risk
Ovarian fibroma, ascites, right pleural effusion

idea.rule: Dextrocardia, sinusitis, bronchiectasis, immotile sperm = dynein defect.
also: Low nasal nitric oxide is a screen

set_title: Pediatric airway signs: Steeple sign, Thumb sign, Tripod position, Inspiratory whoop and Sniffing position
stem: A 2-year-old boy has 2 days of rhinorrhea followed by a barking cough and inspiratory stridor that worsens at night. Temperature is 38.0 C. He is alert and not drooling. An AP neck radiograph shows tapering of the airway just below the vocal cords.
oneliner: 2-year-old boy, barking cough, stridor + subglottic narrowing on AP neck film → ?

whyNot.A: Thumb sign is a swollen epiglottis; his AP film shows **subglottic tapering**
whyNot.B: Tripod is a posture of leaning forward; his finding is **subglottic narrowing on film**
whyNot.C: Whoop follows paroxysmal coughing; he has **a barking cough and stridor**
whyNot.E: Sniffing position is a posture; his finding is **subglottic narrowing on film**

why: Parainfluenza infection narrows the subglottic airway into a pencil-point steeple on the AP film. **Barking cough, stridor and no drooling** indicate croup.

idea.rule: Barking cough + subglottic tapering on AP film = steeple sign, croup.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Subglottic narrowing on AP neck film
Swollen epiglottis on lateral neck film
Sits leaning forward, braced on hands
Neck flexed, head extended, chin forward

set_title: Nail signs: Clubbing, Koilonychia, Beau lines, Mees lines, Nail pitting and Terry nails
stem: A 66-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history has had 4 months of cough, hemoptysis and a 7-kg weight loss. His fingertips are bulbous, and the angle between the nail and the proximal nail fold is lost. A chest x-ray shows a right hilar mass.
oneliner: 66M, 50-pack-year smoker + bulbous fingertips, lost nail fold angle → ?

whyNot.B: Koilonychia is spoon-shaped nails; his fingertips are **bulbous with lost nail fold angle**
whyNot.C: Beau lines are transverse grooves; he has **bulbous fingertips**
whyNot.D: Mees lines are white transverse bands; his nails show **bulbous tips and lost angle**
whyNot.E: Terry nails are white with a red band; his fingertips are **bulbous**

why: Bulbous fingertips with loss of the nail fold angle are clubbing, driven by platelet-derived growth factor and VEGF. A **smoker with hemoptysis and a hilar mass** suggests lung cancer.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Loss of nail fold angle, bulbous tips
Nail growth arrest: chemotherapy, severe illness
Small punched-out pits in nail plate
White nail with thin distal red band

idea.rule: Bulbous fingertips, lost nail fold angle = clubbing = hypoxia or lung cancer.
also: Also seen in cyanotic heart disease and IBD
